oldPassage.text:
| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [../specs/workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](../specs/seat-binding.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [../specs/seat-binding.md](../specs/seat-binding.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Identity (foundation; today the local session writer id) | Foundation authority for identities, today for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-identity` (`packages/identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs`. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`, route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`; Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [identity/spec.md](identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one vector file run by cargo), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; Node reaches it only through the in-process door (`src/native/door.mjs` → `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`, six exports, at most 60 lines, no `/proc`, no `process.kill`); reconcile imports the thin client. Callers reclaim only on `dead` and count a process stopped only after a `sent` signal and a `dead` judgement; `unknown` always holds. Loader errors `process-door-unavailable` and `process-door-not-shipped` fail closed with a next step. No Node file judges a recorded process or signals a bare pid: the only `process.kill` calls left signal the process group of a child the same code just spawned, and the remaining `/proc` readers (lock-holder fd scan, doctor checks, confinement probes) are listed with their reasons in `test/process/one-door.test.mjs`, which fails on any other site. The doctor row kept is `process-containment`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`). A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22, implementation not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22, implementation not started) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. | Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. | Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. | Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22, implementation not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22, implementation not started) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. any red vector or a red sibling check fails, unavailable fails, since activation refuses the same result and there is no run-time switch that disables borrowing; runs on Windows with its own pid-handle assertion), `lock-holders` (for every existing lock file of the locks this release cut over, including the main checkout, merge slot and worktree-admin files, the holders the kernel lists: a holder whose origin is foreign (neither a fgOS process, by the host's state-root pin or a fgOS payload in its argv, nor a borrowed child of that lock) warns with pid and cmdline; a predecessor record next to a lock file naming a domain that is not empty, an unknown record version or a Windows job the host does not judge empty warns with the domain and the reason; the state and porting-events hot records of the workspace, under .fgos/locks, warn with the path and the fence command of the lock verb when a record does not parse or its holder cannot be placed for more than five minutes (absent, alive or dead holders pass; no automatic fix, because a person confirms the holder is gone); holders that cannot be listed are informational), `dependencies-installed`, `gate-bypass-configured`, `claude-plugin-marketplace`, `plugin-skill-cli-reachable`, `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (tsk-32b), `changelog-unreleased-stale`, `herdr-launcher-configured`, `herdr-web-dashboard-configured` (tsk-48w), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `invariant-checks-configured` (tsk-516), `invocation-git-write-grants` (warns when an invocation or executor still grants a git add or git commit tool; the runner commits, workers only edit files; read-only, never rewrites user config), `worktree-setup-configured` (a present worktreeSetup section is a list of non-empty shell commands every runner-created worktree runs after its dependency install; never executes them), `events-jsonl-not-truncated` (tsk-cgg), `worker-slots-ceiling-usable` (tsk-1oz), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `readme-install-tag-exists` (tsk-2t8), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `leaf-notify-drift` (tsk-1el), `task-specs-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-claims-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-type-names-unique` (tsk-397-12; names unique within each tier fgos/agents, domains/*/agents, core/agents, a higher tier replaces a lower one whole, the fgos/agents files checked for shape), `domain-registry-compiled` (every domain's compiled.json file under domains — the precompiled form of the registry and workflow YAML the Work lifecycle reads, regenerated by the build:domains npm script; the check reports a missing, unreadable or stale file and domain YAML that cannot be parsed, and a drift test keeps it equal to the YAML), `dispatch-decide-hook-wired` (tsk-60f; also requires the AskUserQuestion decision-question hook), `codex-hook-wired`, `agy-hook-wired`, `omp-hook-wired`, `pi-hook-wired`, `decision-index-stale` (tsk-1lv-2/tsk-1lv), `advise-execute-capabilities-configured` (tsk-2uf-3), `workflow-capabilities-configured` (every capability a core/domain Workflow unit names resolves in runner.capabilities by exact name or bare verb, the way bind() looks it up, and fails when it does not; one that resolves but has no "prefer" pool on either name is reported as a warning because bind() refuses its unit headless; fgos setup registers every shipped Workflow's capabilities as description-only defaults, so a fresh project starts with that warning, and never overwrites a project's own entry), `capability-serves-valid` (I19: every runner.capabilities entry's serves attribute set is well-formed, no two entries declare the identical set, and the review slot is present), `agy-permissions-configured` (tsk-1xm), `agy-sub-homes-configured`, `bwrap-available`, `curl-available` (curl runs, because fgctl init downloads a release through it; a missing curl is a warning that only blocks the download paths, never a failure, see RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)), `main-checkout-guard-warnings` (tsk-1vc-3), `events-compaction-verified` (tsk-3ve-6), `no-stuck-merge-abort` (tsk-40a), `doc-registry-enforce` (tsk-28x), `doc-registry-stale` (tsk-28x), `doc-alias-broken` (tsk-28x), `doc-active-duplicate` (tsk-28x), `doc-near-duplicate` (tsk-28x), `doc-provisional-aged` (tsk-28x), `doc-topic-oversized` (tsk-28x), `doc-role-underused` (tsk-28x), `doc-source-conservation` (tsk-28x), `doc-current-path-missing` (tsk-3uc), `doc-source-unreachable` (tsk-3uc), `coordination-protocol-fixtures-valid` (retired; confirms legacy definition fixtures retired), `operation-prompt-templates-valid` (Phase 03 I04: every discoverable operation prompt template validates against bounded variables and schema), `coordination-example-requests-valid` (Step 08 Phase 07 R3: published fgos coordination run example request files validate against the same schema boundary the CLI itself enforces, and resolve every referenced protocolRef), `terminal-control` (the terminal-control driver answers through the internal route: driver, declared capabilities and the herdr server incarnation are printed; a missing herdr only warns, a missing layout.geometry capability is information, and a bad FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE fails), `terminal-config` (the terminal section after the merge, each value with its source; fails by name on a grace below the ready timeout plus 30 s, a retain time that is neither null nor a positive integer, an unregistered policy, or limits that are not positive integers or sit below the measured floor of 40x8), `terminal-allocations` (slots past terminal.allocationGraceMs that never launched and retained panes past their time, from the route's reconcile-scan; reports only, closes nothing), `trust-store-readable`, `non-claude-trust-stores-readable` (Phase 07 herdr-trust-supervisor R3: every executor or invocation declaring a codex-toml or agy/agy-json trustStore reads from a store that is actually readable, using the same reader the live dispatch will use), `confined-pane-accounts` (every confined herdr invocation that binds a private home has an account in the machine-global provider account inventory whose credential files exist, so its pane starts logged in; see RUL65b in the runner spec), `agent-cli-project-trusted` (the project root is trusted in every codex home and agy sub-HOME the configured executors run under, so a headless dispatch does not stop at a "Trust this folder?" prompt until its timeout; reads only a yes/no for the one path, names the exact line a person must add, never edits the CLI's config; not applicable when the root is not a git repository or no codex/agy executor is configured), `seat-binding-dry-bind` (binds every seat of every Workflow unit through the runner's own pattern code, in a fixed headless session with no lease, and fails on a policy refusal such as a missing tier cell or an independence rule the pool cannot meet; no pool, account state, tier caps and shared families are information), `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` (for every Workflow unit declared blind, walks each role's candidates through bind() without dispatching anything and fails when the capability prefer pool can bind an executor whose provider family, transport and confinement backend are not in the table of canary-proven pairs kept in the check's own module; read-only, no model call; not applicable when no unit is blind), `executor-posture-coverage` (core capabilities execute, code:implement, and capabilities declaring a pool have at least one candidate executor capable of applying required posture; dry simulation via bind(), no process spawn), `executor-confinement` (dispatch visibility V0 Phase 01 group D: the transport an interactive dispatch needs, a readable folder-trust store so a fresh worktree can be pre-trusted instead of stopping at a dialog, and a second reading of the rule that an executor may only declare bypass permission mode alongside full confinement), `herdr-executor-kinds` (Phase 05 R3: every executor dispatched through a herdr pane names an agent kind herdr can actually start, and none depends on an integration hook herdr reports as outdated -- an installed-but-stale hook is believed by herdr and may report the wrong agent state, while a missing one only degrades detection), `executor-profile-warnings` (Phase 06 executor-policy-dispatch-seams: legacy executor/capability entries hardcoding policy-shaped flags, policy-overrides-as-identity, or account-pool-shaped env, each named with its documented migration target -- informational only, never a hard failure), `active-release-matches-checkout` (read-only Node payload contents against doctor dir working tree, not HEAD or Rust binary freshness; reports changed/missing/extra source files while excluding staged dependencies, skips outside source checkouts and main-owned activation in linked worktrees; use fgos:dev for working-tree code or restage/activate for plain fgos), `rust-host-binary-present`, `rust-host-target-supported`, `legacy-node-payload-present`, `command-routes-drift`, `confinement-policies-declared`, `confinement-backend-registry-readable`, `confinement-bwrap-platform`, `confinement-probe-freshness`, `confinement-blind-read` (a blind unit can be enforced: the registered bwrap backend hides peer run state, homes and processes from a worker; reports pass, fail, or backend-unsupported, in which case every blind unit is refused), `confinement-strict-readiness`, `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` (Phase 04 M8: no confinement temp resource is left behind by a dead owning process, and no confinement temp root is readable beyond its owner; a home kept for a still-open pane is not orphaned; the fix tightens the root to 0700 and reaps), `confinement-herdr-maturity`, `instruction-projections-stale`, `runner-coordination-orgPolicy-shape`, `operation-capability-resolves` (Unit I21: every discoverable operation's declared policy.capability resolves against the live runner config, reporting reachable provider-family diversity), `shadow-binder-divergence` (dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening Phase 7 C1: real PlacementPolicy/ProviderAdapter shadow-binder divergence is durably recorded to a local JSONL under .fgos/dispatch/, not only an ephemeral stderr line; informational, never fails), `observe-dir-writable`, `observe-friction-migrated`, `observe-host-resolvable`, `writer-identity-resolvable` (the writer identity resolves through the Rust host for both the running host and the workspace activation a plain git commit hook uses; each binary is asked directly, so an older activated release shows as a version mismatch), `identity-machine-id` (this machine has an id minted by the Identity component, asked through `fgos identity machine --json`; absent only warns, `fgos doctor --fix` mints it once and never replaces it; an unreadable or invalid file fails), `observe-run-coverage`, `coordination-protocol-dead-vocabulary` (validates definitions against dead vocabulary), `model-policy-tier-coverage` (validates model policies cover the default tier, runner.defaults.tier, for every registered executor), `executor-family-unique` (two agent executors of one provider family fail, naming both), `executor-skills-installed` (every skill an agent executor declares in its supports.skills has a SKILL.md in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout, chosen by each invocation's CLI (claude: .claude/skills, codex: .agents/skills, omp: .omp/skills, pi: .pi/skills, grok: .grok/skills), every invocation of an executor must have the skill; a missing one fails naming the path and the remedy; a CLI with no known skill directory is reported as not checked), `model-policy-pools` (a tier cell entry model@pool whose pool runner.llmAccounts does not declare warns; not evaluated when no cell names a pool), `llm-accounts-shape` (every problem the runner.llmAccounts reader finds fails: an inventory in the project config, a pool name with an at-sign or another spelling of a family, an account without a credentialStore directory), `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` (when runner.llmAccounts is declared, accounts or login directories that differ from runner.providers, which the lease still reads, warn), `global-model-policies-portable` (a list or model@pool cell in the global runner.modelPolicies fails, since older releases on the machine cannot read it), `tier-fallback` (a family `runner.tierFallback` lists for a tier that has no `modelPolicies` cell at that tier, or no agent executor, warns: the walk skips it; never fails), `tier-vocabulary-dead-keys` (validates project and global config do not contain retired tier/rigor keys), `runner-patterns-config` (validates presence, valid checkers, and cumulative checkersByRigor for runner patterns), `runner-generated-paths` (validates runner.generatedPaths source-to-render-target mappings), `process-containment`, `run-supervisor-route`, `runtime-socket-dir`, `run-attempts-stuck`, `gate-kill-grace`, `legacy-attempts-stuck`, `units-awaiting-resume`, `cancel-wait`. The registry is open, but this list is not a snapshot — it names every registered check, and a module adding one updates this row in the same change | yes | — |
| 7b | Doctor fix | One named repair `fgos doctor --fix` can run before re-reporting checks | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`registerFix`), independent of `registerCheck`/`registerConfigDefault` (per tsk-2cs). Today's registered fixes: `credential-copies-retained` (re-checks private homes held after repeated staging failures, and any kept home under a registered backend's own root, which nothing else retries, under the account lock, and removes one only when its login is shown applied or obsolete; also removes an interrupted staging (pending/.tmp-*) only after claiming it by rename, when its writer is gone and it is empty, identical to a copy already kept, or shown no newer than the source login under the account lock; never removes on age), `gate-bypass-configured` (tsk-2qz, the registry's first entry to register all three capabilities at once), `claude-plugin-marketplace` (tsk-4xg), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `bin-discovery-cache` (tsk-2qc-1), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `decision-index-stale` (tsk-1lv-2/tsk-1lv), `agy-permissions-configured` (tsk-1xm), `no-stuck-merge-abort` (tsk-40a), `doc-registry-stale` (tsk-28x), `confinement-backend-registry-readable`, `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` (Phase 04 M8), `terminal-dir` (creates the terminal directory under the state root with mode 0700 when missing, and tightens an existing one to 0700), `lock-dirs` (creates the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root with mode 0700 when missing, and tightens an existing one to 0700, since the first lock taken before setup may have created it with the umask's mode), `instruction-projections-stale`, `runner-coordination-orgPolicy-shape`, `project-fgos-launcher`, `dispatch-decide-hook-wired`, `codex-hook-wired`, `agy-hook-wired`, `omp-hook-wired`, `pi-hook-wired`, `runtime-socket-dir`, `run-attempts-stuck`, `legacy-attempts-stuck`. Same rule as #7: the registry is open, but this list names every registered fix and a module adding one updates this row in the same change | yes | — |
| 7c | Doctor check `process-containment` | Which process-containment driver this machine would pick for an attempt (`bwrap-pidns`, `linux-pgroup`, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), the level it gives and the named escapes; read from the host route's `--protocol 1 --probe` answer (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` §14, `docs/platform/process/spec.md` §10) | passed with `kernel`; warning with the name `best-effort` (Linux without a user namespace, macOS); never a failure for being best-effort | yes (computed) | — |
| 7d | Doctor check `runtime-socket-dir` | The run supervisor's runtime socket directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fgos`, else `/tmp/fgos-<uid>`): exists, mode 0700, owned by the user, short enough for a unix socket path. `fgos setup` creates it; the fix creates it too | passed / failed (missing, wrong owner or mode, too long) | yes (computed) | created by setup |
| 7e | Doctor check `run-attempts-stuck` | Runs with an envelope v3 and no `closed.json` whose attempt lock is free, counted by `fgos internal adopt --scan --probe-only` (writes nothing, takes no lock); the fix drives them to closed through the one sweep (`sweepAttempts`) | passed / warning with the count | yes (computed) | — |
| 7f | Doctor check `run-supervisor-route` | The active host binary answers `--protocol 1 --probe` with `result: ok` for each of `fgos internal supervise`, `gate`, `adopt`, `attempt-step` | passed / failed naming the route or the protocol mismatch | yes (computed) | — |
| 7g | Doctor check `gate-kill-grace` | The config key `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` (the SIGTERM to SIGKILL grace of the launch gate): value and source (`project`, `global`, `default`); project overrides global; setup does not write the key into the global config until every workspace runs a release that knows it | passed with the value (absent: default 10000); failed when not an integer or below 1000 | yes (computed) | 10000 |
| 7h | Doctor check `cancel-wait` | The config key `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (how long a controller stopped by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM waits for its attempts' receipts), read by the same reader as `gate-kill-grace`: value and source (`project`, `global`, `default` = grace + 5000); an unusable value, below 1000 or shorter than the grace, fails | yes (computed) | — |
| 7i | Doctor check `legacy-attempts-stuck` | Runs from before the run supervisor still `running`: fails while one is provably dead (every recorded pid dead, no version-1 home), warns with the reason for each run that is kept; fix settles the provable ones as `abandoned-legacy` | yes (computed) | settled in `run.json` by fix |
| 7j | Doctor check `units-awaiting-resume` | Unit runs whose controller is gone and whose last attempt is closed, with the `fgos run --resume <unit>` command; warns, never fails | yes (computed) | — |
| 8 | Output rendering mode | How `fgos setup`/`fgos doctor` present their result | enveloped JSON (every other verb's shape, unchanged) / colored plain text (`--pretty`) | yes | enveloped JSON |
